item.title: Solar Time and Standard Meridians

item.sequence_title: Evolution of Names for the Indian Subcontinent
stages: 1. Sapta Sindhava (Vedic period): Reference to the land of seven rivers in northwestern India.
2. Jambudvīpa (Ancient texts): Textual name describing the southern continent shaped like a jamun leaf/fruit.
3. Bhārata / Bhāratavarṣha (Puranas & Epics): Name associated with the ancient King Bharata and the people living south of the Himalayas.
4. Hi(n)du / Indoi (Persian & Greek texts): Phonetic evolution derived from the River Sindhu (Indus).
5. India, that is Bharat (1949 Constitution): Modern constitutional synthesis uniting historical identity with modern republic.
1. Primary Stage: Forestry workers harvest timber trees and extract wood pulp from forests.
2. Secondary Stage (Paper Mill): Industrial workers process pulp into large paper rolls.
3. Secondary Stage (Printing Press): Printers bind text and images onto paper to assemble textbooks.
4. Tertiary Stage (Logistics & Distribution): Transport trucks deliver books to warehouses and retail stores.
5. Tertiary Stage (Retail): Bookstores sell finished textbooks directly to students.
1. Early Phase: Agricultural settlement expansion and copper metalwork development.
2. Mature Phase (2600–1900 BCE): Flourishing urbanism with brick architecture, grid streets, and global maritime trade.
3. Late / De-urbanisation Phase (post-1900 BCE): River course changes and climate shifts lead to rural migration.

item.category: The Three Levels of Governance in India
items: 1. National / Central Level: Governs the entire country (headquartered in New Delhi).
2. State Level: Governs individual states (e.g. Karnataka, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu).
3. Local Level: Governs local villages (Panchayats) and urban cities (Municipalities).

item.category: The Three Tiers of Panchayati Raj
items: 1. Gram Panchayat (Base Tier): Village-level elected council headed by a Sarpanch.
2. Panchayat Samiti (Middle Tier): Block-level council coordinating multiple Gram Panchayats.
3. Zila Parishad (Apex Tier): District-level council overseeing regional development.

item.category: The Three Types of Urban Local Bodies

item.category: The Five Tamil Sangam Tiṇais (Ecological Zones)
items: 1. Kuriñci: Mountainous zone associated with hunting and gathering.
2. Mullai: Pastoral forest zone associated with cattle rearing.
3. Marutam: Wetland river valley zone associated with agriculture.
4. Neytal: Coastal zone associated with fishing and salt extraction.
5. Pālai: Arid desert zone associated with dryland survival.
